{"researchQuestions":["Can an unsupervised autoencoder trained solely on unlabelled Modbus and BACnet traffic flag anomalous sequences, measured against scripted fault injections on the university testbed?","Does an 8-bit quantised and pruned model retain detection performance on BACnet traffic, measured against AUROC on a scripted BACnet fault-injection set created on the university testbed?","Does an incremental online model maintain F1 score within an accepted tolerance across a defined concept-drift scenario replayed from the eighteen months of historical logs, measured against a static model retrained on the full log over the same window?","Does the deployed model on the EdgeWatch sensor achieve a false-positive rate below a threshold agreed with the company, measured against four weeks of live traffic on one customer site?"],"plan":[{"phase":"Phase 1 — Data preparation and architecture selection (months 1–3)","work":"University research staff parse and segment anonymised logs from three sites; university PI selects baseline model architecture using testbed Modbus and BACnet captures; company engineers validate protocol parsing against EdgeWatch output. University staff create scripted Modbus and BACnet fault-injection sets on the testbed.","result":"A labelled testbed dataset with scripted fault injections for both Modbus and BACnet, and a selected model architecture, documented in a technical report delivered at M3."},{"phase":"Phase 2 — Quantisation and ARM prototype (months 4–6)","work":"University research staff apply 8-bit quantisation and structured pruning to the chosen model and evaluate AUROC against the scripted BACnet fault-injection set; company engineers integrate the model into the EdgeWatch firmware build; inference latency and memory footprint measured on EdgeWatch hardware.","result":"A quantised model prototype running inference on the ARM target, with a benchmark report covering AUROC on the BACnet injection set and latency and memory use, delivered at M6."},{"phase":"Phase 3 — Drift evaluation and field pilot (months 7–9)","work":"University PI replays a defined concept-drift scenario extracted from the eighteen months of historical logs and compares the incremental model F1 score against a static retrained baseline over that window; company field technicians deploy the prototype on one customer site and monitor false-positive rate.","result":"A drift evaluation report covering the replayed historical window and a false-positive rate benchmark from four weeks of live traffic on one customer site, delivered at M9."},{"phase":"Phase 4 — Integration and delivery (months 10–12)","work":"University PI and company security engineers resolve issues identified in the pilot; university research staff finalise model training pipeline and documentation; company engineers complete EdgeWatch integration and acceptance testing.","result":"A deployable model package, integration guide, and final technical report delivered at M12, with a peer-reviewed paper submitted to a relevant venue."}],"candidate":""}
